title: Hackers Hit Supermarket Fridges Across Europe, Spoiling Food
summary:
A hacking attack spread across Europe on Monday, hitting supermarket fridges and freezers from Sweden to Belgium and forcing stores to throw away spoiled food.

The attack raised temperatures in refrigerator and freezer units at dozens of stores. It hit supermarket groups Ahold Delhaize and Colruyt in Belgium and Luxembourg, as well as Swedish grocers ICA and Coop. Furniture-to-meatballs retailer Ikea also saw at least one store affected.

At an ICA franchise store in Stockholm, sales manager Engla Ingwall said the attack occurred at 2 a.m. but was only noticed hours later. "Everything is destroyed," she told Reuters during a visit to the store. "There has been a cyberattack and all our freezers reached 50 degrees [Celsius]."

A spokesperson for privately held ICA said the company was aware that a limited number of stores were affected by an incident overnight that impacted their refrigeration and freezer systems.

The incidents echoed an attack in France last month, when police said hackers seized control of cooling units at hundreds of supermarkets, causing fires and food losses. Ahold Delhaize also reported a cybersecurity incident to police last month.

No one has claimed responsibility for either attack. The incidents have heightened concerns among European authorities about hybrid threats to infrastructure amid growing security tensions since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Moscow has repeatedly denied involvement in sabotage or hybrid warfare operations. Reuters could not establish who was behind Monday's attacks or whether they were linked to the incidents in France.

"It is not known who is behind this attack, and it may never be determined," said Katrien Eggers, spokesperson for Belgium's Centre for Cybersecurity. She said she was concerned about the growing number of incidents, in part due to artificial intelligence. "All IT systems are potentially vulnerable, and AI can now be used to successfully exploit these weaknesses - especially by sophisticated actors," she said.
why_it_matters: Food stores depend on computer-controlled cold storage, so an attack on fridges can waste food across many countries at once and raise wider worries about the safety of everyday systems.

background_read: A cyberattack happens when hackers break into computer systems to damage them or take control of them.
Many supermarket fridges and freezers are now connected to computers, so their temperatures can be watched and changed from far away.
Cold food must stay cold to stay safe to eat, so when a fridge warms up, the food inside can spoil and must be thrown away.
Authorities worry about attacks on important systems like food stores because problems there can affect many people at once.
